A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RelayFormer. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, are readable and support comparison across renaming and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original image and video localization results, component ablations, robustness tests, and computational evaluations, including an appendix layer-replacement study.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds cross-dataset F1 evaluations on AutoSplice, CocoGlide, and Defacto-12k in Appendix A.6.

M1.justification: The core attention, query-decoder, and loss equations remain. V2 omits v1's explicit one-shot reuse of first-frame queries without explaining whether that procedure was abandoned. Its new Algorithm 1 repeats first-frame patches, contradicting Section 3.1's per-frame extraction. These inconsistencies prevent reliably distinguishing procedural changes from documentation errors.

E1.justification: V2 adds actual evaluations on AutoSplice, CocoGlide, and Defacto-12k in Table 9, substantially broadening image-forgery distributions, particularly to AI-generated manipulations. The original image benchmarks and DAVIS-to-MOSE video evaluation remain.

E2.justification: The corresponding image, video, complexity, and robustness comparisons retain their baseline sets. New Table 9 evaluates IML-ViT, SparseViT, and Mesorch, all already compared in v1; extending them to new datasets does not introduce new comparison methods.

E3.justification: Appendix A.4 changes the stated image sub-image size from 512×512 to 528×528 and per-GPU batch size/accumulation from 2/8 to 4/4, retaining effective batch size 64. V2's main text still specifies 512×512, leaving the actual setting unresolved. The clip-length sweep is removed; retained benchmark protocols otherwise remain largely stable.

E4.justification: V1 Figure 5's one-shot decoding analysis across clip lengths 4, 8, 16, and 32 disappears. Token-count, decoder, spatial/temporal, resizing, layer-replacement, and corruption analyses remain. The attention visualizations move into v2's appendix rather than constituting new analyses.

E5.justification: Both Appendix A.4 sections mention seed 42 and report medians of three runs with different seeds. Neither version adds confidence intervals, dispersion estimates, or significance tests; the new results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 9 adds results across three datasets, with average F1 scores of 0.303 for Relay-ViT and 0.372 for Relay-Seg. Tables 1 and 4 revise Relay-ViT's average from 0.543 to 0.554, but reported settings also change, preventing a same-setting improvement claim. The one-shot results disappear; Relay-Seg's original benchmark scores and Table 2's video results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 replaces the stride-independent unit-count expression with stride-aware counts for overlapping sub-images and explicitly defines the dimensional decomposition and rotations of 4D RoPE. These are limited mathematical refinements; the attention/loss equations and complexity analysis remain substantively equivalent, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: V2 withdraws the explicit one-shot video-decoding and linear-decoder claims promoted in v1's abstract, introduction, and conclusion. Its central claims of unified image/video localization, resolution adaptivity, efficiency, and state-of-the-art performance remain.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands the scientific interpretation: Appendix A.1 identifies reduced precision for cross-sub-image dependencies relative to full attention; Section 3.2 and A.2.2 explain local/global parameter specialization; A.6 attributes AI-forgery performance differences to backbone inductive biases. These mechanisms and applicability qualifications were absent from v1.

D1.justification: V2 adds substantial implementation documentation: extraction pseudocode, explicit 4D RoPE construction, 16-pixel overlap, LoRA rank 8 and scaling factor 2, application to QKV projections and feed-forward networks, unmerged trainable backbone weights, and relay-token padding for batching. It also states that code accompanies supplementary material. Some new instructions conflict with the main text.

R1.justification: V2 adds Poth et al. on Adapters and removes the Dosovitskiy, Vaswani, and Xie references, while emphasizing comparison with SparseViT in its motivation. The image/video related-work surveys remain largely unchanged. Table 2 newly cites FOCAL as Yang et al., conflicting with its Wu et al. attribution in related work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, conclusion, and substantial method passages are rewritten. GRT/GLoRA becomes GLR/GLRA, Local Unit Construction becomes Input Unification, and the appendix is extensively reorganized into numbered subsections, with existing analyses moved and explanatory material expanded.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. Figure 1 gains a local/global illustration, Figures 2–3 are redrawn, Table 3's subtables are merged, and Table 4 is simplified. V2 expands the dataset table, adds Table 9, removes the one-shot plot, and relocates retained attention figures.

improvement.justification: The additional AI-forgery evaluations, implementation specifics, and concrete limitation strengthen coverage and explanation. However, v2 removes the one-shot decoding evidence and introduces consequential documentation conflicts: 512 versus 528-pixel sub-images and first-frame repetition in Algorithm 1 versus per-frame extraction in Section 3.1. These affect reproducibility and identification of the evaluated procedure, leaving the net quality change uncertain.
